name: Mount Gower
note: Mountain: the island's highest peak (875 m), climbed by an 8-hour guided day walk with rope-assisted sections; the tourism board calls it one of Australia's best day walks. Guide required.

name: Mount Lidgbird
note: Mountain: the second big peak beside Mount Gower, with a track Wikipedia names; not promoted by the island's walking list or Wikivoyage.

name: Ball's Pyramid
note: Sea stack: the world's tallest sea stack, about 23 km south-east of the island, seen by boat tour and reached by dive trips; no landing. Visitors go for the view and the diving.

name: Ned's Beach
note: Beach: the island's north-east beach and its snorkelling jewel; visitors wade in to hand-feed fish from the food dispenser and walk the Malabar track from it.

name: Blinky Beach
note: Beach: a secluded surf and swim beach on the west coast, reached by walking from Transit Hill or Lagoon Road; the tourism board lists it as a top beach for surfing, picnics and fishing.

name: Old Settlement Beach
note: Beach: a southern beach with weather-sculpted sandstone rocks, a picnic area and the start of the Max Nichols track; green turtles graze the sea-grass off it, and the Catalina wreckage is behind it.

name: North Bay
coordinates_source: osm natural=beach 'North Beach' (approximate; North Bay picnic area is nearby; judge to confirm)
note: Beach: a secluded north-coast bay reached only on foot or by water, with picnic and barbecue facilities and toilets at its picnic area. Coordinates are the nearby OSM North Beach, approximate.

name: Middle Beach
note: Beach: the central beach on the lagoon side, where the Clear Place walk starts; it sits by the museum and the township.

name: Lagoon Beach
note: Beach: the sandy beach along the lagoon shore, reached by the foreshore walk; a stroll and swim beach with banyan trees and pandanus along the front.

name: Boat Harbour
note: Cove: a sheltered small cove on the south-east coast at the end of the coastal track; the walk from Lagoon Road is the way in.

name: Muttonbird Point
coordinates_source: osm tourism=viewpoint (Mutton Bird Point Viewing Platform)
note: Lookout: a headland lookout on the coastal track (about 1.4 km in) with a view across to Muttonbird Point and the seabird colonies.

name: Malabar Hill
note: Hill: a 208 m ridge-top walk above Ned's Beach with red-tailed tropicbird views over the cliffs; the island's most popular walk, to Pooles Lookout and the Dawsons Point ridge.

name: Pooles Lookout
note: Lookout: a viewpoint on the open grassy slope of the Malabar walk, before the summit; part of the Malabar Hill walk.

name: Kim's Lookout
note: Lookout: a clifftop viewpoint on the Malabar ridge walk, past Malabar Hill, looking over the seabird cliffs; some cliffs on the island walks are unfenced.

name: Mount Eliza
note: Hill: a 147 m rocky summit reached by a steep 0.6 km walk from North Bay; sooty terns nest along the trail, so it closes to the public from September to March.

name: Intermediate Hill
note: Hill: a 250 m summit on the coastal track with a viewing platform and some of the island's best views, including Ball's Pyramid.

name: Transit Hill
note: Hill: a central summit with a 360-degree lookout platform, reached by an easy 1.2 km walk through palm forest; it links on to Blinky Beach.

name: Goat House Cave
note: Cave: a cave on Smoking Tree Ridge reached by a steep 2.1 km walk with rope-assisted sections; a difficult walk rather than a cave tour.

name: The Clear Place
note: Walk: a clearing in the palm forest reached by an easy 1.2 km return walk from Middle Beach, past a large land slip; the diversion to Valley of the Shadows is part of the same walk.

name: Valley of the Shadows
wiki: Valley of the Shadows, Lord Howe Island
note: Valley: a short side diversion on the Clear Place walk, down into a small valley just before The Clear Place.

name: Stevens Reserve
note: Reserve: a 1.2 km return loop walk with interpretive signs through the forest, starting by the boat sheds on Lagoon Road.

name: Old Gulch
note: Cove: a small rocky cove reached by a short level 0.3 km boardwalk from North Bay.

name: Max Nichols Memorial Track
note: Walk: a 1.5 km track over the ridge from Old Settlement Beach to North Bay, with steps; a moderate ridge walk and part of the island's walking network.

name: Little Island
coordinates_source: osm place=islet (track end is nearby; judge to confirm the visitor point)
note: Walk: an easy 3 km return track on an old service road through forest to a grassy clearing on the southern end of the lagoon, the furthest point before the Mount Gower guide route.

name: Lord Howe Island Museum
note: Museum: island history and world-heritage exhibits, with a visitor centre; entry by donation, open 9am to 3pm daily on Wikivoyage's listing.

name: Catalina Wreckage
coordinates_source: osm historic=memorial (Catalina crash memorial by the bike parking)
note: Heritage wreck: the remains of a Catalina flying boat that crashed on the lagoon, still lying on the Malabar ridge above Old Settlement Beach; a monument stands by the bike racks.

name: Lord Howe Island Botanic Gardens
note: Garden: a small botanic garden on Lagoon Road, past the museum; Wikivoyage notes the whole island is effectively a botanic garden.

name: Lord Howe Island Permanent Park Preserve
wiki: Lord Howe Island Permanent Park Preserve
note: Nature reserve: the protected park covering about two thirds of the island, where the walks run; a park area rather than a single place.

name: Lord Howe Island Marine Park
note: Marine park: a managed marine area of about 46,000 hectares around the island, where the snorkelling, diving and fishing take place; a zone rather than one stop.

name: Erscott's Hole
note: Snorkel site: a reef site off the airport with about 500 fish species and 90 coral species, a fair swim or a boat trip from shore; the island's best accessible snorkelling.

name: Comet's Hole
coordinates_source: osm tourism=viewpoint 'Comets Hole' (approximate; judge to confirm the snorkel point)
note: Snorkel site: a spot about 100 m offshore from the airport runway, Wikivoyage's best spot for Galapagos sharks; a snorkel or dive site rather than a landing.

name: Admiralty Islands
note: Islands: a volcanic group about 15 minutes by boat from Lord Howe, with pinnacles and reefs for diving and snorkelling; visited by boat tour and dive trip.

name: Blackburn Island
note: Island: a small islet in the Lord Howe group, named in Wikipedia's geography category; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Wolf Rock
note: Rock: an offshore rock in the Lord Howe group, named in Wikipedia's geography category; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Erskine Valley
note: Valley: a valley on the island listed in Wikipedia's geography category; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Lord Howe Island Weather Station
note: Visitor attraction: the weather station's balloon launch runs twice daily (summer 10:15am and 4:15pm; winter 9:45am and 3:45pm, per the tourism island directory); whether the public can watch on site is unconfirmed.
